capabilities.title: Grid search enumerates the full cartesian product of a discrete configuration space
capabilities.rationale: Both SDKs pass this fixture through their public optimize entry point with algorithm "grid": Python SDK tests/unit/parity/test_conformance_grid.py (Traigent develop bf57c2b5) and the JS SDK parity conformance test (develop cb4fa5de). Both assert raw invocation count, no duplicates, set equality, and max-trials truncation. Parameter ordering is not part of the contract.

capabilities.title: Multi-objective min-max normalization, sum-to-one weighting, zero-span fallback and dominance guard
capabilities.rationale: Both SDKs pass this fixture through public APIs: Python SDK tests/unit/parity/test_conformance_multi_objective.py (Traigent develop f7f0f47d) via ObjectiveSchema.from_objectives, OptimizationResult.score_trials and traigent.optimize; JS SDK parity conformance test (develop 25e4a855) via the public scoreTrials export and optimize. Both assert normalized weights, per-trial normalized and weighted scores within 1e-9, the unique-max best trial, and the 0.99 dominance guard.

capabilities.title: Stop limits: maximum trials, cumulative cost cap and maximum total examples

entryPoints: @traigent/sdk optimize({ budget: { maxCostUsd }, execution: { maxTotalExamples } }) with maxTrials

capabilities.rationale: Both SDKs pass this fixture through public APIs: Python SDK tests/unit/parity/test_conformance_stop_limits.py (Traigent develop 75d8b33f) via traigent.optimize(max_trials, cost_limit, max_total_examples); JS SDK tests/parity/conformance-stop-limits.test.ts (traigent-js develop 9e30c534) via optimize with maxTrials, budget.maxCostUsd and execution.maxTotalExamples. Both assert trial counts, stop reasons, rows per trial and best accuracy within 1e-9, and reject invalid limits and negative trial costs. Plateau stopping, cost estimation, a default cost cap, failed-trial handling, a grid exhausted exactly at a limit and precedence between simultaneous limits remain out of scope until the owner-ruled target rules are implemented.

capabilities.title: Stop rules: failed trials, default cost cap, plateau, stop precedence and pre-trial cost estimate

entryPoints: @traigent/sdk optimize({ budget: { maxCostUsd } }) with maxTrials and .optimize({ plateau: { window, minImprovement } })

capabilities.rationale: Both SDKs pass this fixture through public APIs: Python SDK tests/unit/parity/test_conformance_stop_rules.py (Traigent develop 1e7e30bf) via traigent.optimize(max_trials, cost_limit, max_total_examples, plateau_window, plateau_epsilon); JS SDK tests/parity/conformance-stop-rules.test.ts (traigent-js develop 94c2710e) via optimize with maxTrials, budget.maxCostUsd, execution.maxTotalExamples and plateau. Both assert trial counts, stop reasons, trial statuses, rows per trial and best accuracy within 1e-9, and reject a capped run with no reported cost. Not asserted: the label of a stop when the grid is exhausted exactly at a limit, wallclock limits, Python-only stop conditions, and sub-tolerance running-best improvements, where Python gates its best by the tolerance and JS keeps a plain running best.
